entries.plain: Shows a value on the screen. Whatever you put inside the parentheses is written to the output.
Pauses the program and waits for the person to type something. The typed text comes back as a string. Run these programs in the terminal with F6.
Starts a function: a named block of code you can run later by calling its name.
Sends a value back out of a function and stops the function at that point.
Runs the indented block only when a condition is true.
Means "else if": tries another condition when the previous ones were false.
Runs when the matching if (and any elif) conditions were all false.
Repeats a block once for each item in a collection, or for each number produced by range().
Repeats a block as long as a condition stays true. Make sure the condition can eventually become false.
Creates a sequence of numbers. range(3) gives 0, 1 and 2; the end value is not included.
Tells you how many items are in a list, string or other collection.
An ordered collection written with square brackets. You can add, remove and change items.
A collection of key/value pairs written with curly braces. Look up a value by its key.
A piece of text. Strings are written inside quotes.
A whole number with no decimal point, such as 3 or -12.
Brings in another module so you can use the tools it provides.
Starts a block where an error is allowed. A matching except block handles the error instead of crashing.
Catches an error raised inside the matching try block so the program can keep going.
The boolean value meaning yes. Its partner is False.
The boolean value meaning no. Its partner is True.
Means "no value here yet". It is different from 0, an empty string, or False.
A string prefixed with f that lets you put expressions inside curly braces.
